subject: 95% credible intervals for annual occupancy estimates

messages.author: b4d2eae4afc10686
messages.subject: 95% credible intervals for annual occupancy estimates
parts:
I feel like this should be an easy problem to solve but can't figure it out for some reason. I am trying to obtain 95% credible intervals around each year's estimated psi value when using the tPGOcc model. For example, I get the annual average psi of model (out) using:

psi.avg<-apply(out$psi.samples,3,mean)

To get the credible intervals I thought it should be something like:

psi.CRI<-apply(out$psi.samples,3,function(x){quantile(x,probs=c(0.025,0.975))})

However, this gives me intervals that span basically 0-1 in most years which didn't seem right. My model showed convergence based on rhat and had okay Bayesian p-value (0.16) so I wouldn't have thought the CRIs would have been that wide but maybe I'm missing obvious here. Any thoughts either confirming I did this incorrectly, or that it is correct and that I should investigate the model fit further would be greatly appreciated.

Tom

messages.author: 0b274a0ee3490d75
messages.subject: Re: 95% credible intervals for annual occupancy estimates
parts:
Hi Tom,

Based on what you described, it sounds to me like you want to determine the average occupancy probability across all your sites in each year, and then get a credible interval around that average. To get the means, the approach you used is just fine, but the credible intervals need to be calculated in a slightly different way. You should first calculate (for each MCMC iteration), the average occupancy probability across all sites in each year. Then you can use that to get the 95% credible interval for "average occupancy probability in each year". Here's some code that should allow you to do that, and explore how the two approaches give different values for the credible intervals. So, the thing I call "psi.mean.quants" below is what I think you want.

# Posterior samples of the average occupancy across all sites within each year
psi.mean.samples <- apply(out$psi.samples, c(1, 3), mean)
psi.means <- apply(out$psi.samples, 3, mean)
psi.mean.of.means <- apply(psi.mean.samples, 2, mean)
# psi.means and psi.mean.of.means will be the same
all.equal(psi.means, psi.mean.of.means)
# However, the same is not true for the quantiles
psi.quants <- apply(out$psi.samples, 3, quantile, c(0.025, 0.975))
psi.mean.quants <- apply(psi.mean.samples, 2, quantile, c(0.025, 0.975))
psi.quants
psi.mean.quants

Jeff
